experiment.purpose: Compare Lodgepole and Orange under equivalent 64-component terminal addressability.

next_gate.hypothesis: Non-contiguous wedges derived from representation structure may concentrate useful information better than contiguous terminal blocks.

not_supported: Forest V2 does not justify Orange as a distinct architecture when wedges are ordinary contiguous 64-component blocks.
Forest V2 does not test semantic or learned wedges.
supported: Equivalent 64-component addressability removes the meaningful Orange advantage observed in V1.
Contiguous structural wedges and Lodgepole blocks are functionally equivalent under this benchmark.
Forest V1's partial-access advantage was primarily caused by asymmetric access granularity.
